summary: Mettanando Bhikkhu is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg, studying under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel.

Michael Alram is a historian, archaeologist, and specialist in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. After studying at the University of Vienna (~1977–1982), he held posts there (~1986) and at the Kunsthistorisches Museum (~1982–2020).

Michael Aris was a scholar of Tibetology and history who studied at Durham University and SOAS, University of London under David L. Snellgrove. He held posts at Wolfson College, St Antony's College, and Oxford, as well as Harvard.
Michael Balk is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He was a doctoral student at the University of Bonn until 1988 and held a post at the Berlin State Library, attested in 1991.

Michael Baxandall studied at Downing College (~1951–1954). He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum (1961–1965), the Warburg Institute (~1965–1986), Cornell University (~1982–1983), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1986–1996).

Michael Carrithers is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post at Wolfson College, Oxford in 1977 and served as Lecturer in Social Anthropology at Durham University (~1984–1992).

Michael Chase is a philosopher who studied at the University of Victoria and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1993–1997). In ~2002, he became a researcher in ancient philosophy at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique.

Michael Comans works in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and completed his doctorate under Jan Willem de Jong at Australian National University (~1984–1987), later holding posts at Sydney and Sri Venkateswara Temple.

Michael Como specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kuo-liang Wang and advisers Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and held an attested post at Columbia University in 2009.

Michael D. Willis, an Indologist and historian of Buddhist studies, studied at Victoria and Chicago. His career included posts at British Columbia, SUNY New Paltz, De Montfort, the British Museum (1994–2014), and the European Research Council (2014–2020).
Michael Friedrich is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Friedrich Alexander Bischoff and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from approximately 1994 to 2023.
Michael G. Morony is a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley (~1957–1961) and UCLA (~1961–1972), where he later served as professor from ~1974 to 2015.

Michael Hahn (1941–2014) was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Göttingen, Marburg, and Bonn under Wilhelm Rau and Franz Bernhard. He held posts at Bonn, the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, SOAS, Ryukoku, and Marburg.

Michael Hookham is a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner and scholar who studied under traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa (1965) and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at SOAS and the University of London between 1977 and 1984, becoming Lecturer in Nepali at SOAS around 1987.

Michael J. Sweet (d. 2021) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD at Wisconsin–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, studying also with several traditional teachers, and later held clinical psychiatry appointments there.
Michael J. Tetreault is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned a Master of Arts at San Diego State University under the supervision of Sandra A. Wawrytko, attested in 2011.

Michael J. Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Cape Town (~1986–1989) and the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1991–1994), completing his doctorate under William F. Powell (~1994–2000).

Michael K. Jerryson was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed undergraduate studies at Wisconsin–Madison under Harold Scheub. He held professorships in religious studies at Eckerd College (~2008–2012) and Youngstown State University (~2012–2021).
Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.
